h1: ibis Bangkok Riverside — A Riverside Pool with Chao Phraya Sunset Views, at Budget Prices
intro: On the west bank of the Chao Phraya River in the Charoen Nakhon district sits a 3-star hotel that budget travellers keep recommending — ibis Bangkok Riverside delivers something rare in Bangkok: a riverfront swimming pool with Chao Phraya views at Economy prices, no five-star bill required. 266 rooms across 7 floors, free shuttle to BTS Krung Thonburi every 30 minutes, and a 10–15 minute walk to ICONSIAM. Standard rooms start from approximately THB 1,300/night, river-view rooms a little more. Score 8.8/10 from 1,241 verified reviews.
galleryAlts: ibis Bangkok Riverside outdoor pool overlooking the Chao Phraya River at dusk, with the opposite bank lit up
Standard room at ibis Bangkok Riverside — 21 sq m, clean and bright, ibis-standard double bed
TASTE restaurant at ibis Bangkok Riverside serving breakfast buffet and Thai-international cuisine throughout the day

body.html: If there is one thing guests single out most at ibis Bangkok Riverside, it is the outdoor pool perched right on the Chao Phraya River — around 25 metres of clean water facing the waterway, with the opposite bank reflected in the surface. Come sunset, the light turns amber across the river and people who have just checked in tend to stand there taking photos for far longer than they intended. Reviews consistently describe it as "a resort-feel pool at an Economy hotel price," which is about as good a one-line summary as you will find.

Rooms come in five types, all built around a compact 21 sq m footprint (the Family Room is 31 sq m): Standard Double, Standard Twin, Standard Double River View, Standard Twin River View, and Family Room. The river-view categories add only THB 200–300 per night, yet the difference is significant — morning light off the water and an evening ritual of watching boats pass make that small premium feel like a bargain. Every room carries the familiar ibis kit: flat-screen TV, mini-fridge, work desk, kettle, and free Wi-Fi; housekeeping earns consistently high marks.
"Pool is well-maintained, never crowded. The sunset over the Chao Phraya from the poolside is something else — didn't expect this from a budget hotel at all."

The hotel sits at 27 Soi Charoen Nakhon 17, on the Thonburi side of the river — roughly 10–15 minutes on foot along the riverside path to ICONSIAM, or a short Chao Phraya Express Boat hop. The free shuttle to BTS Krung Thonburi runs every 30 minutes, connecting to the BTS Silom Line for Sathorn, Surasak, Saphan Taksin, and beyond. The Charoennakorn pier nearby opens up the waterway: Wat Arun, Wat Pho, Maharaj, and Asiatique in the evening are all reachable without touching a Grab.

The TASTE restaurant handles an all-you-can-eat breakfast buffet — eggs to order, ham, pancakes, pastries, fruit, and coffee. Reviewers call it "adequate rather than exciting," but nobody leaves hungry. The 24-hour bar is a reliable late-night option for those who come back after exploring Asiatique. Staff earns some of the warmest praise in any review category — "friendly, genuinely helpful, great at recommending where to eat and how to get around" appears in review after review, across all languages.

Honest caveats worth knowing: rooms are genuinely small. At 21 sq m the layout works fine for one or two light packers but feels cramped with large suitcases open. Bathrooms are compact to match. Some reviews mention thin soundproofing — early-morning river boat traffic can filter through windows that do not open. Rooms also lack in-room slippers and robes (request them at reception — standard Economy-tier ibis globally). The pool area has limited changing facilities and showers beside it.

Stepping back: ibis Bangkok Riverside punches above its price class because of location, the riverside pool, and staff attitude — a combination that genuinely sets it apart from other budget hotels in the city. A score of 8.8 from over 1,200 reviews (Location 9.1 / Service 8.8 / Cleanliness 8.9 on Trip.com) tells you these guests are not just tolerating the place. For anyone who wants a Chao Phraya riverside experience without spending five-star money, this is one of Bangkok's most practical answers.

highlights.title: Riverside Pool on the Chao Phraya
highlights.text: Approx. 25-metre outdoor pool facing the river directly. Sunset views praised by nearly every reviewer — an unusual find at Economy prices.

highlights.title: Free BTS Shuttle Every 30 Minutes
highlights.text: Free shuttle to BTS Krung Thonburi connects the Silom Line seamlessly. Pier nearby for Chao Phraya Express Boats to Asiatique, Wat Arun, Wat Pho.

highlights.title: Walk to ICONSIAM in 10–15 Minutes
highlights.text: Charoen Nakhon riverside location puts ICONSIAM within a pleasant walk along the river. Wat Arun, Grand Palace, and Asiatique all accessible by boat.

honestSummary: ibis Bangkok Riverside delivers a Chao Phraya riverfront pool and sunset views at Economy rates — its strongest suits are location, the pool, and staff warmth. Weaknesses are compact room sizes standard for Budget ibis globally, and thin soundproofing. If you want large rooms or total silence, look elsewhere; if riverside atmosphere at an honest price is the goal, this hotel genuinely delivers.
honestChecks: Travelling with lots of luggage or as a family needing space? — The 21 sq m standard rooms will feel cramped with two large suitcases open. Only the Family Room (31 sq m) gives meaningful extra space → book Family Room well in advance, or consider Ramada Plaza Menam Riverside nearby for more generous room sizes.

Relying on public transport frequently during your stay? — Waiting up to 30 minutes for the free BTS shuttle can be frustrating during rush hours → keep Grab as a backup (approx. THB 40–60 from BTS Krung Thonburi to the hotel), or plan your outings around the shuttle timetable.

Keen on a river-view room specifically? — City View rooms don't see the river at all; River View must be booked explicitly → the premium is just THB 200–300/night and the payoff — especially at sunset — is absolutely worth it.

tips.title: Always Book a River View Room
tips.body: The upgrade is only THB 200–300 per night. Waking up to the Chao Phraya outside your window — and watching the sun set from your room — makes that extra spend immediately obvious.

tips.title: Plan Around the Free Shuttle
tips.body: The free BTS Krung Thonburi shuttle runs every 30 minutes. Time your outings to match the schedule and save significantly over several nights — or keep Grab as a backup for off-schedule moments.

tips.title: Use the River Pier for Sightseeing
tips.body: The Charoennakorn pier near the hotel puts you on the Chao Phraya Express Boat network. Wat Arun, Wat Pho, Maharaj, and Asiatique at night are all reachable cheaply and more enjoyably than by road.

tips.title: Hit the Pool at 5 PM
tips.body: Between 17:00 and 18:30 the riverside pool gets the best light of the day — golden hour over the Chao Phraya with boats drifting past. Bring your camera.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — ibis Bangkok Riverside

faq.q: Where is ibis Bangkok Riverside located and how do I get there?
faq.a: The hotel is at 27 Soi Charoen Nakhon 17, Charoen Nakhon Road, Banglamphulang, Khlong San, Bangkok 10600 — on the west bank of the Chao Phraya River. A free shuttle runs every 30 minutes to BTS Krung Thonburi (Silom Line). Grab from the BTS station to the hotel costs approximately THB 40–60.

faq.q: What are ibis Bangkok Riverside room prices and what types are available?
faq.a: Prices start from approximately THB 1,300/night for Standard Double (city view). River View rooms add around THB 200–300. The Family Room (31 sq m) runs approximately THB 2,200/night. Prices rise during high season and public holidays.

faq.q: Does ibis Bangkok Riverside have a pool? Is the view good?
faq.a: Yes — there is an outdoor pool of approximately 25 metres, overlooking the Chao Phraya River directly. The sunset view is consistently the most praised feature across all reviews. The pool is well-maintained with ample sun loungers.

faq.q: How close is ibis Bangkok Riverside to ICONSIAM? How do I get there?
faq.a: ICONSIAM is around 10–15 minutes on foot along the riverside walkway or a 5-minute Grab ride. The Charoennakorn pier near the hotel also has Chao Phraya Express Boats heading to Sathorn Pier (BTS Saphan Taksin) and the ICONSIAM pier.

faq.q: Who is ibis Bangkok Riverside best suited for?
faq.a: Best for couples, groups of friends, and budget-conscious travellers who want a genuine riverside Bangkok experience without paying luxury prices. Families should book the Family Room. Not ideal for those who need large rooms or very quiet surroundings.
